Our two steeplechasers Eddie Short and Pete Baganll, finished 3rd and 5th after taking a horrible bashing in the process. It is a pity that some of our longer distance track men don't display courage of this sort and help Belgrave to once again take its place at the front in distance running.

Eddie Short who had taken fourth place in the Steeplechase last year, ran again. He said that he was not so fit as last year but was running gamely.

Eddie Short ran well against Birchfield's ace Freddie Green and finally Jack Brown took us to within 5 seconds of winning the event on that last stage with his Club Record breaking run.
In the Junior race Eddie Short was again our first man home in 7th position, and to gain such a high place in this race speaks well for Eddie's strength and determination.

In the Junior race Eddie Short again ran well ... he was our first man home in 13th place. C.W.Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first “open” race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit.

We are sorry to record the death last November of Eddie Short, a regular in our running teams after the war. Eddie served in the RAF where he also played rugby but he got away from camp as often as possible to race for the Bels.

We heard with sadness during the year of the deaths of Charlie Jones, Frank Jarvis and Win Shepherd, who were Presidents of the Club in 1959/60,1966/67 and 1990/91 respectively, and also of Don Brown, Daye Donovan, Len Herbert and Eddie Short.
